title: Hosted API Endpoint Family: Gating, Dependency Management, and Gradual Launch Runbook
creator: Asha Kapur
description: Purpose: Define a product requirements document and an operational runbook that govern gating criteria, cross-team dependencies, and a staged rollout for the new unified hosted API endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). This PRD focuses on launchability: what must be true before we enable the new surface for tenants, how to coordinate Dedicated/Private teams and infra, and the automated/operational checks required to safely expand traffic. Scope: requirements for gating checks, compatibility mapping for legacy endpoints, rollout sequencing, monitoring and rollback criteria, docs and migration guidance. Success metrics: zero-sev launch for first 10 enterprise customers, <5% error rate on 95th-percentile latency at day-7, and successful canary-to-global promotion within 48 hours of no regression detected.
requirements: Unified endpoint contract documented with per-method schemas (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) and example payloads
Backward compatibility shim: legacy endpoint redirectors translate common older parameters to new surface for first 90 days
Gating checks: API conformance tests, token-based auth validation, quota/enforcement layer smoke tests, and end-to-end large-model inference sanity (sample prompt matrix) must pass in staging
Infra readiness: Dedicated capacity autoscale policy validated for 2x expected initial QPS and fallback routes configured
Observability: per-route SLO dashboard + alerting (5xx rate, p95 latency, cold-start ratio) wired into PagerDuty
Docs: Developer migration guide, SDK snippets for Node/Python, changelog and deprecation timeline published
Security: KMS integration verified for Private customers and SAML-based RBAC checks for enterprise tenants
out_of_scope: Dedicated customer onboarding automation beyond capacity validation
Full SDK language coverage at GA (we will ship Node/Python first)
acceptance_criteria: All automated e2e conformance tests pass in staging for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank
Canary traffic (1% of global traffic) shows no increase in 5xx and <3% increase in p95 latency for 48h
Migration docs published and validated by internal Solutions Engineers with a test customer
Legacy redirector feature toggled and tested with synthetic workloads; deprecation flag works per-tenant
Runbook steps for rollback and emergency mitigations written and playbook-tested in a fire drill
rollout_checklist: Pre-launch: API contract sign-off by API guild and external review (Confluence PRD link)
Pre-launch: Security review and penetration test sign-off
Pre-launch: Infra autoscale + fallback routing rehearsal completed
Canary day-0: Enable endpoint in region-us with canary flag = 1% traffic
Canary day-1: Run targeted prompt set (latency/cost/quality) and compare to baseline; validate traffic shaping behavior
Canary day-2: If no regressions, increase canary to 10% and run chaos tests (delay injected on one AZ)
monitoring: Dashboards: per-route p50/p95/p99 latency, token-cost trends, error breakdown by code
Alerts: p95 latency > 2x baseline for 15m, 5xx rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m
Quality monitors: sampling of replies against golden prompt set with automatic regression scoring
Cost monitor: token-per-request moving average compared to expected profile; alert on >20% delta
dependencies: ENG-39102 (Routing: fallback policy and region-aware routing)
PM-49870 (Docs: Migration guide and SDK snippets)
risks: Model-quality regression on rare prompt patterns undetected by standard prompt sets
Unexpected cost spike from caching behavior mismatch in production
Dependency failure: Dedicated autoscale misconfiguration causing throttling during ramp
mitigations: Add focused quality sampling for long-tail prompts and higher frequency checks during canary
Cost guardrails: hard token-rate limit and automated scaling budget cap for initial 30 days
Pre-launch run of Dedicated autoscale with synthetic spike test at 3x baseline and postmortem review
timeline: 2025-03-10: Global rollout target (subject to canary success)
